Subject: RoadSafe pilot blueprint & risk register — next steps

Hi Oliver / Sandra —

Thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have a single source of truth heading into the pilot kickoff: 

Summary of ask:
- RoadSafe wants a 6-week pilot to validate real-time incident triage (low-latency generation + vector search) against 3MB/day of telemetry logs.
- Success criteria should map to product and ops owners (latency, recall, business reduction in manual triage).

Proposed success criteria (first pass):
- 95th percentile generation latency < 350ms for 512 token context
- Mean reciprocal rank (MRR) on 3 canonical use-cases >= 0.72
- False positive triage rate < 6% against RoadSafe test set
- Demonstrated 20% reduction in human triage time across 100 sample incidents

Ownership & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria & access (RoadSafe to provide sample telemetry + SSO service account).
- Weeks 1–3: integration + staging runs (Redwood SEs + RoadSafe infra).
- Weeks 4–5: production-like throughput test & quality evaluation.
- Week 6: readout + decision.

Risks we flagged on-call (brief):
1) Data access delay — RoadSafe infra team needs to enable a read-only S3 service account or provide a streaming endpoint.
2) Vetting telemetry PII — security wants a checklist and signed DPA addendum.
3) Edge-case model hallucination on cryptic logs — need a small evaluation prompt set to measure.

Action items (owner in parens):
- Provide sample telemetry dataset (Oliver) — due Tue 3/14
- Provide list of security requirements / contacts (Sandra) — due Tue 3/14
- Redwood to send pilot playbook + risk register draft (Priyom + Marissa) — done (attached)

I attached the pilot playbook (v1) and a blank risk_register CSV. Please review and reply with any additional criteria or timing constraints.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Priyom Das

Hi team —

I reviewed the sample payload Oliver described and sketched a tech-first risk register. Main technical blockers to flag now: 

A) Authentication & network:
- If RoadSafe prefers streaming via a websocket, we need a short-lived token flow and an allowed IP list for our staging cluster (Owner: RoadSafe infra).
- If S3, the service account must have ListBucket + GetObject on the prefix (Owner: RoadSafe infra).

B) Data characteristics & tooling:
- Logs include base64-encoded blobs in ~12% of events — we need a small parser spec to avoid feeding binary into the model (Owner: Marissa).
- Sample size: 3MB/day target is fine, but 95th percentile message length spikes will impact both latency and cost. Recommend a capped preprocessor to trim to canonical fields (Owner: RoadSafe / Redwood).

C) Quality measurement risks:
- We should lock 8 canonical evaluation scenarios (happy/path + 7 edge cases). Without those, MRR comparisons will be noisy (Owner: Oliver + Priyom).

Mitigations proposed:
- Temporary preprocessing lambda to normalize events (Redwood provides starter code).
- Short-term KV cache set to 60s for repeated context to reduce token usage on duplicate events.
- Escalation path: any P0 model hallucination -> immediate rollback to smaller model variant and paged alert to Ben (SE lead) if repeat >3 in 24h.

I'll attach the draft risk_register CSV with these rows filled in. Priyom — we should add SLA exception language for the rollback path in the playbook.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick note on escalation & a potential high-severity blocker: 

Marissa flagged the base64 blobs in logs — our staging run yesterday showed that if the preprocessor fails for >2% of events, we observe cascading parsing exceptions that can slow throughput and produce malformed context. That's a P0 for the pilot.

Immediate mitigations I want in place before kickoff: 
- Redwood to deploy the preprocessing lambda as a tunable blue/green job (Marissa) — target Mon 3/20 EOD.
- RoadSafe to set a short-term circuit-breaker: if parsing error rate > 2% in a 5-minute window, pause ingestion and alert both teams (Oliver).
- If circuit-breaker trips >2 times in a 24-hour period, we escalate to execs and consider pausing the pilot until fix (Ben).

Priyom / Oliver — please confirm you can commit to the two mitigations above. If not, we'll need to push kickoff until the protections exist.

Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
